spec.description: Health of the pathfinder full node that backs the validator. The Status row answers whether anything is wrong. The rows below it are collapsed on purpose and only need to be opened when the Status row turns red.

spec.title: In sync
spec.description: OK means the node is no more than two blocks behind the chain. Anything else shows how many blocks behind it is.

spec.title: Hung submissions, last 24h
spec.description: Submissions that hung within the last 24 hours. OK means none did. The Gateway Submission Hung alert rule uses a ten-minute window, so it clears long before this panel does: the alert answers whether a hang is happening now, this panel whether one happened today. The running total since the node started is in the Gateway row below.

spec.expr:
clamp_min(
  (sum by (network) (gateway_requests_total{method="add_transaction", network=~"$network"}) - sum by (network) (gateway_request_duration_seconds_count{method="add_transaction", network=~"$network"}))
  -
  (sum by (network) (gateway_requests_total{method="add_transaction", network=~"$network"} offset 24h) - sum by (network) (gateway_request_duration_seconds_count{method="add_transaction", network=~"$network"} offset 24h)),
  0
)

spec.title: Restarts, last 24h
spec.description: OK means the node has not restarted in the last 24 hours. A restart resets every counter on this dashboard to zero. The network name is derived from the scrape port, because this metric carries no network label: 9000 is mainnet, 9001 is sepolia.

spec.title: Local head block
spec.description: Latest block stored locally, shown as a full number. A counter: it only rises.

spec.title: Process uptime
spec.description: Time since the pathfinder process started; resets to zero on restart. The network name is derived from the scrape port, because this metric carries no network label: 9000 is mainnet, 9001 is sepolia.

spec.title: Sync lag over time
spec.description: Normal is 0 to 2 blocks. Measured over 30-31 August the value never reached 3, the dashed red line, on either network. Spikes that fall back to zero are normal; a rising staircase is not.

spec.title: Blocks processed per second
spec.description: Normal is 0.5 to 0.6 per second on both networks, with occasional brief dips to about 0.35. Flat zero while sync lag grows means block processing has stalled.

spec.title: Block pipeline timing
spec.description: Four gauges pathfinder exposes for the most recent block; the unit is assumed to be seconds. Typical values measured over 30-31 August: block_time 2 s on both networks, block_latency 4-5 s, block_download 1-2 s on mainnet and about 1 s on sepolia, block_processing tens of milliseconds. Two-day peaks: latency 13 s, download 8 s.

spec.title: Block processing time
spec.description: Summary quantiles over block processing time. Typical values measured over 30-31 August: mainnet p50 about 60 ms and p99 about 120 ms, sepolia p50 about 22 ms and p99 about 95 ms. Two-day peaks reached 1.2 s on mainnet and 600 ms on sepolia.

spec.title: Hung submissions since node start
spec.description: Running total of attestation submissions that never came back. It only resets when pathfinder restarts, so a non-zero number here is history, not a live problem.

spec.expr: sum by (network) (gateway_requests_total{method="add_transaction", network=~"$network"}) - sum by (network) (gateway_request_duration_seconds_count{method="add_transaction", network=~"$network"})

spec.title: Hung submissions over time
spec.description: Each step up is one attestation submission that left the node and never came back. A flat line means nothing new hung; the line only falls when pathfinder restarts.

spec.expr: sum by (network) (gateway_requests_total{method="add_transaction", network=~"$network"}) - sum by (network) (gateway_request_duration_seconds_count{method="add_transaction", network=~"$network"})

spec.title: Gateway failures by reason
spec.description: Stacked count per bucket, grouped by network and reason; the method is dropped to keep the series count readable and is available on hover. The absolute height depends on the selected range, because a wider range means wider buckets. Reason starknet is the constant background: it runs all the time on both networks, does not affect sync, and can be ignored. Reason timeout is the one that matters: it is rare, and both real block stalls of 30-31 August had a timeout burst in the same minute. Reasons decode and rate_limiting have stayed at zero.

spec.title: Gateway latency, slowest 1 percent
spec.description: Only requests that finished are counted here; a request that never finishes never appears on this panel. Typical values are under 300 ms. Peaks measured over 30-31 August: 4 to 5 s on mainnet and up to 6.5 s on sepolia, on the block and state-update methods. add_transaction usually reads zero because submissions are rare.

spec.title: Calls from the attestation tool
spec.description: Calls the attestation tool makes into this node. Typically under 0.02 calls per second per method. A burst an order of magnitude higher accompanies the retries that follow a hung submission.

spec.title: Time to accept a submission
spec.description: Time the node takes to accept a submission from the tool, p50 and p99 from the RPC histogram. Usually near zero. Over 30-31 August three spikes reached about 10 s.

spec.title: RPC failures in range
spec.description: One number per failing method over the selected range; empty means no RPC call from the attestation tool failed. Measured over 30-31 August: 27 failures on starknet_estimateFee with error kind transaction_execution_error, and a starknet_addInvokeTransaction series with kind unexpected_error that exists but did not increase in range. Neither cause has been established.

spec.title: Node stall, last 24h
spec.description: Shows the clock time of the last moment in the past 24 hours when the node stopped receiving blocks. OK means there was no such moment. The time is local, same as the dashboard axis, so it can be found directly on the graphs below. Checked every 20 seconds, so a stall shorter than a minute cannot slip between two checks. The bar is fewer than 10 blocks a minute; normal is about 35, and a slow patch of the chain itself sits at 15 to 20, so the two do not overlap. Measured over 30-31 August: two real stalls, one per network, both caused by Starknet timing out, both followed by a catch-up burst above 70 blocks a minute. Nothing here can be fixed locally; the panel exists to explain a lost epoch after the fact.

spec.title: Node running
spec.description: Whether Prometheus can reach the pathfinder process right now. DOWN means the process is gone or its metrics port is closed, and the other panels on this dashboard go stale rather than red. The network name is derived from the scrape port, because this metric carries no network label: 9000 is mainnet, 9001 is sepolia.

spec.title: Pathfinder Node Health
